My dear Miss Yonge	
[I](/person/939) have given our printer orders to go on with the '[Clever Woman](/book/58)'. I hope you will receive proofs at once & have a rapid supply. It will make some such work as '[The Trial](/book/53),' as you wish.
I have corresponded with a friend of yours about '[Events of the Month](/periodical/69).'[^1] I think the idea admirable the want is a crying one. But it should be [illegible] and well carried out. I hardly see my way to the right plan.
I have several times wished there was a [Don Quixote](/organisation/32) in our Series. I see you have been telling the story briefly, and you recommend the one in Unwin’s Englishman’s Library. Is it very well done? I almost wish you would do it some day. But we should not lose sight of the more important book
ever dear Miss Yonge
Yours faithfully
A. Macmillan


[^1]: It seems that CMY had suggested to the [Henrietta Murray](/person/1073), the editor of Events of the Month that Macmillan might take it over from the Mozleys who published the last number in January 1865..
